newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit record close in upbeat mood.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit record close in upbeat mood.

text.p: Swiss shares posted a second straight record close on Wednesday, with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) establishing itself firmly above the level of 5,200 that it hurdled on Tuesday, dealers said.
Prices came down slightly in late trade due to a weaker Wall Street start. "But let's not forget the SMI added more than 160 points in the past two sessions," one trader said.
Prospects remained bright thanks to the firming U.S. dollar and low interest rates, he added. "There is enough money around still waiting to be invested," he noted.
The SMI ended up 31.3 points, or 0.6 percent, at 5,238.5, while the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 22.34 points, or 0.6 percent, to 3,313.71.
Bourse volume was a moderate 2.41 billion francs.
One dealer said there was some profit-taking in financials, whereas industrials were generally lifted by a firming dollar.
Bank shares were surrounded by recurring rumours of takeovers, spin-offs, mergers and restructuring, dealers said.
UBS bearers fell 10 francs to 1,591, while most-active CS Holding jumped seven francs, or 3.76 percent, to a closing high of 193.25.
Novartis registered shares were among the few losers among blue chips. The stocks ended down one franc at 1,987 due to profit taking. Roche was up 125 francs at 13,160.

Alusuisse ended with a gain of six francs to 1,396 after surging to an all-time high of 1,414 francs in early trade. Old rumours regarding a possible spin-off of one of Alusuisse's units led to soaring demand, dealers said.
Sulzer, Holderbank, Ciba and Baloise were among the biggest winners among blue chips.
